paper.title: OS-Copilot: Towards Generalist Computer Agents with Self-Improvement
paper.central_claim: OS-Copilot provides a unified OS-level agent framework (planner, configurator memory, actor with critic/refiner); FRIDAY built on it self-improves through self-directed learning that accumulates agent-generated tools, outperforming prior GAIA systems by 35% on level 1 and mastering unfamiliar applications (Excel 0%->60% on SheetCopilot-20, PowerPoint qualitatively) with minimal supervision.

provenance.notes: actual_model/session_id/receipt_ref are not exposed to the worker agent; model_type follows the claude-kimi type overlay (haiku slot -> claude-sonnet-5-5[1m]) as dispatched by the controller.

rationale: agent生成并经LLM评分(>8)留存的Python工具库，GAIA测试集上学习消融仅约+4题(L1/L2)，SheetCopilot-20 0→60%；无统计/预算匹配/工具级验证，主增益多来自框架本身。

evidence.quote: We use OS-Copilot to create FRIDAY, a self-improving embodied agent for automating general computer tasks.
evidence.support_explanation: Central framing: framework plus a self-improving agent.

evidence.quote: On GAIA, a general AI assistants benchmark, FRIDAY outperforms previous methods by 35%, showcasing strong generalization to unseen applications via accumulated skills from previous tasks.
evidence.support_explanation: Headline claim; the 35% is relative to GPT-4 Plugins (human-selected plugins) on level 1.

evidence.quote: In the current implementation, tools scoring above 8 are preserved by updating the tool repository in procedural memory (step ⑦).
evidence.support_explanation: Admission rule: LLM critic generality score > 8 after a judged-successful execution.

evidence.quote: In this example, no suitable tools are identified (similarities below a specified threshold), prompting activation of the Tool Generator to devise an application-tailored tool for the current subtask (step ③).
evidence.support_explanation: Tool generation is triggered by retrieval miss (threshold unspecified).

evidence.quote: The FRIDAY will iterate through steps ④ to ⑥ until the subtask is considered completed or a maximum of three attempts is reached.
evidence.support_explanation: Refiner repairs action/tool/subtask from execution errors and critic feedback, up to three attempts.

evidence.quote: With a pre-defined learning objective, such as mastering spreadsheet manipulation, FRIDAY is prompted to propose a continuous stream of tasks related to the objective, spanning from easy to challenging.
evidence.support_explanation: Practice curriculum is self-proposed but conditioned on a human-set objective.

evidence.quote: We initialize FRIDAY with four basic tools and facilitate its exploration of the dev set of GAIA to accumulate more tools (result in 9 more tools).
evidence.support_explanation: GAIA tools are harvested from the dev set; the test set is separate.

evidence.quote: Subsequently, we evaluated FRIDAY’s performance on the test set by submitting our results to the official evaluation server
evidence.support_explanation: Held-out private test scored by the benchmark's server.

evidence.quote: significantly outperforming the popular AutoGPT-4 system (14.4%)
evidence.support_explanation: Text reports AutoGPT-4 L1 14.4% while Table 1 lists 15.05%: reporting inconsistency.

evidence.quote: FRIDAY w/o learning 36.56 17.61 6.12 FRIDAY 40.86 20.13 6.12
evidence.support_explanation: Learning ablation on GAIA test: L1 36.56->40.86, L2 17.61->20.13, L3 6.12->6.12.

evidence.quote: Initially, FRIDAY, without self-directed learning, is unable to complete any tasks and tends to use the pandas and matplotlib packages for spreadsheet control, resulting in failures.
evidence.support_explanation: The 0% baseline fails because of library choice; a knowledge-injection explanation is not ruled out.

evidence.quote: to generate 10 tasks about manipulating Excel using the propenyxl package
evidence.support_explanation: Self-generated practice tasks name the openpyxl package (spelled 'propenyxl' in the paper), i.e. the key hint is in the practice prompt.

evidence.quote: FRIDAY then solves these 10 tasks and autonomously accumulates 8 tools
evidence.support_explanation: Practice yields 8 tools; evaluation on the 20-task SheetCopilot-20 subset.

evidence.quote: SheetCopilot † GPT-3.5-Turbo 40% Claude 45% GPT-4 55% FRIDAY (w/o learning) GPT-4 0% FRIDAY GPT-4 60%
evidence.support_explanation: Pass@1 on SheetCopilot-20: FRIDAY 60% (12/20) vs w/o learning 0% vs SheetCopilot-GPT-4 55%.

evidence.quote: denotes the results reported in
evidence.support_explanation: SheetCopilot rows are copied from Li et al. 2023, not re-run under matched conditions.

evidence.quote: Also worth noting that FRIDAY achieves such a level of proficiency by solving and learning on just 10 tasks.
evidence.support_explanation: Small practice set; no repeated practice runs reported.

evidence.quote: In our qualitative analysis, we design a task to create a PowerPoint slide to introduce OS-Copilot.
evidence.support_explanation: PowerPoint evidence is a single qualitative task (Fig 4).

evidence.quote: Assessing the successful completion of a given subtask is challenging due to the absence of ground truth.
evidence.support_explanation: Admission signal is an LLM judgement acknowledged to lack ground truth.

evidence.quote: we manually verified the correctness of all 93 level-1 tasks and assigned capability labels.
evidence.support_explanation: Level-1 test set has 93 tasks, so 36.56% = 34/93 and 40.86% = 38/93.

evidence.quote: GPT-4 Plugins rely on humans to browse and select proper plugins based on the task question.
evidence.support_explanation: Baselines are not budget- or information-matched to FRIDAY.

evidence.quote: The discrepancy between FRIDAY and AutoGPT-4 underscores the importance of self-criticism and refinement.
evidence.support_explanation: Component attributions are inferred from cross-system comparison, not ablated.

evidence.quote: Although none of these components are first innovated in this paper, OS-Copilot organically combines them into a cohesive whole
evidence.support_explanation: Authors state the components (planner, critic, refiner, memory) are not new.

evidence.quote: executing in 105 seconds compared to more than 500 seconds in the case of AutoGPT-4
evidence.support_explanation: Text says 105 s; Table 3 lists FRIDAY L1 as 118 s: second reporting inconsistency. Cost is reported as time only.

evidence.quote: Due to the limited budget, we use GPT4-turbo-1106 in FRIDAY.
evidence.support_explanation: Single backbone; no token or dollar accounting.

evidence.quote: Notably, all the atomic operations and tools in SheetCopilot are manually crafted and verified, whereas FRIDAY autonomously generates all tools used.
evidence.support_explanation: The library source is the agent, not a human (domain failure F3 absent).

evidence.quote: particularly their reliance on prompt engineering and their incapacity when confronted with closed-source applications
evidence.support_explanation: Authors' stated limitation.

evidence.quote: However, assessing the successful execution of these subtasks poses significant difficulties due to the absence of ground truth.
evidence.support_explanation: Sub-task evaluation relies on rules or LLMs, potentially inaccurate (authors).

evidence.quote: Additionally, while executing tasks in the GAIA development set, FRIDAY generates a set of tools that exhibit a degree of atomicity and universality.
evidence.support_explanation: Tool lists (Tables 10-12) show generic file/CSV/JSON readers and Excel/PPT helpers; tool invocation counts on test tasks are not reported.

evidence.quote: We seed OS-Copilot with 4 manually created tools for basic computer functionalities, such as web browsing and speech-to-text translation
evidence.support_explanation: Seed library is manual; growth is agent-generated.

signatures.object: Tool repository in procedural memory: agent-written Python tool classes (plus API services) retrieved by dense similarity
signatures.information: Subtask from the DAG planner, OS/system info, working directory, retrieved tool docs, execution outputs, critic judgement; no ground-truth labels
signatures.operation: On retrieval miss the Tool Generator writes a tool class and invocation; Executor runs it; Critic judges completion and scores generality 1-10; Refiner repairs the action/tool/subtask up to 3 times
signatures.output: New or revised tool code; stored if critic score > 8
signatures.conditions: Executable OS environment; tasks that need app-specific scripting (openpyxl, python-pptx)
signatures.feedback: Execution errors plus LLM critic analysis
signatures.selection_rule: LLM critic completion=true and generality score > 8 (threshold ad hoc); no replay, dedup or increment test described
signatures.persistence: Tool files in the repository; later self-correction updates tool code
signatures.later_use: Dense retrieval of tools into the configuration prompt for later subtasks
signatures.claimed_effect: GAIA test L1 36.56->40.86, L2 17.61->20.13 with learning; SheetCopilot-20 0%->60%
signatures.failure_boundary: Weak web/multimodal tools, closed-source GUI apps, prompt-reliance; backbone changes cause large swings

signatures.object: Self-directed learning curriculum: tasks proposed by the agent for a human-set objective, solved by trial and error
signatures.information: Pre-defined learning objective (e.g. spreadsheet manipulation); GAIA dev questions for the GAIA run
signatures.operation: Propose easy-to-hard tasks, solve them with the S1 loop, accumulate tools and semantic knowledge
signatures.output: 8 Excel tools from 10 self-generated tasks; 9 tools from GAIA dev; PowerPoint tools from further practice
signatures.conditions: Practice tasks disjoint from the evaluation tasks (dev vs private test; self-generated vs SheetCopilot-20)
signatures.claimed_effect: Mastering unfamiliar applications with minimal supervision

gap.author_gap: Existing language agents target a single app or terminal, and hand-crafting tools and prompts for the many OS applications is impractical; AutoGPT lacks self-directed learning of unfamiliar applications.
gap.checked_gap: Real limitation (fixed, human-designed tool set per application) but the specific change here, agent-generated tool library via practice, is the Voyager-style move ported to OS/Python tools; the paper states novelty mainly as integration.
gap.lineage: AutoGPT/OpenAgents multi-scenario agents -> Voyager-style self-directed skill learning (Minecraft) -> OS-level agent with generated Python tools; SheetCopilot as manually tooled spreadsheet specialist
gap.closest_adjacent: Voyager (named, not compared), AutoGPT, GPT-4 plugins, SheetCopilot; other tool-making agents are not discussed
gap.residue: Generalising to unfamiliar apps without per-app engineering
gap.stakes: Hundreds of OS applications cannot each get bespoke tools
gap.method_response: Retrieval-miss tool generation plus practice-time library growth with critic gating
gap.remaining_gap: Admission is judgment-based; no tool-level validation; benefit on GAIA is small and unreplicated; web/GUI apps unsupported
unresolved: Voyager and other skill-library agents are not in the pinned materials; novelty relative to them is not independently assessed.
